items.title: Glamorgan Archives items catalogued but not yet viewed: 1975 County Treasures survey, East Vale Local Plan, civic society files and 1971 aerial photographs
items.holder: Glamorgan Archives (open to view in the search room; catalogue entries read, items not yet seen)
items.basis: cross-reference (Glamorgan Archives catalogue entries CVG/EC/3/1/3/13, CVG/EC/3/1/3/1, D387, D1824/4/5, D1824/4/1, D1824/3/7 and D978/3/2/24-26, read 31 October 2026)
items.why: Seven entries in the Glamorgan Archives catalogue describe records bearing on the house and its setting between 1971 and 1992. The catalogue descriptions have been read; the items themselves have not been seen, so what they show is not checked. CVG/EC/3/1/3/13, ‘Photographs of sites in sector 7 of Penarth survey’ (c1975, one bundle), lists ‘Tymawr Farm, Llandough’ among the sites photographed for the South Glamorgan County Treasures survey, alongside School House, St Dochdwy Church and Llandough House. Our inference, not checked: this is Ty Mawr (Great House Farm), not Llandough Farm, and it may be the survey behind the ‘County Treasure’ description of the house relayed in December 1988. CVG/EC/3/1/3/1 probably holds the matching survey form (not checked). D387 holds the Penarth Town Council provisional list for the County Treasures survey, 1975. D1824/4/5, in the Penarth Civic Society planning papers, holds the East Vale Local Plan of 1987 and its 1991 review, with correspondence; a copy would fill MR-0044, whose catalogue entry is at present a placeholder. D1824/4/1 is a file headed ‘CADW’ (November 1990 to March 1992) and D1824/3/7 is the society’s correspondence of 1988-1992. D978/3/2/24-26 are aerial photographs taken on 6 July 1971 of Llandough Hospital and the area towards the Llandough trading estate; whether the farmhouse is in frame is not checked. Parcel: A (the farmhouse) for the survey photograph, form and list; parcel not identified for the local plan, the civic society files and the aerial photographs (the plan’s proposals map and the photograph frames would identify it).

items.title: Ownership of the 0.74 ha Leckwith Road objection site beside the former quarry (open question)
items.holder: HM Land Registry (title register and plan, if registered); Vale of Glamorgan Council (planning register and the 1992 appeal file); the planning inspectorate’s appeal decision (not checked)
items.basis: cross-reference (Vale of Glamorgan Unitary Development Plan, Inspector’s report volume 2, C13.3.2 and C13.3.4)
items.why: The Inspector’s report on objections to the Vale of Glamorgan Unitary Development Plan (volume 2, section C13.3) records objection 232.4 by the Land Division of the Welsh Development Agency, seeking a housing allocation for ‘an area of land measuring about 0.74ha and located on the northern fringe of Llandough’. The report describes it as ‘a sloping area of pasture land with sporadic tree cover’ that ‘abuts Leckwith Road’, with its north-eastern boundary ‘formed by the upper lip of a former quarry/brickworks site now occupied by the Llandough trading estate’, and adds that ‘a previous Inspector also reached a similar conclusion when dismissing an appeal on this site in 1992’. Who owned the site, and whether it was ever part of Great House Farm, is not shown: an objector is not necessarily the owner. Open question: who held the title when the 1992 appeal and the plan objection were made, and whether the land appears in any earlier conveyance of the farm. Parcel not identified: the plan’s objection-site map, the 1992 appeal decision or the registered title plan would identify it.
refs: Vale of Glamorgan Unitary Development Plan, Inspector’s report on objections, volume 2, C13.3 (objection 232.4)
Planning appeal on the same site dismissed in 1992 (reference not yet found)

items.title: Measured drawings of Great House Farm beyond the 1974 ground plan: first floor, roof, heights, the farm ranges and the yard (open question)
items.holder: Not known. Possible holders: RCAHMW (National Monuments Record), Glamorgan Archives (1975 survey photographs, 1971 aerial photographs), Welsh Government (aerial photography), the press photograph collections
items.basis: cross-reference (RCAHMW NA/GL/88/49 and NA/GL/89/208; the 1974 record card; Cadw photographs of 29 July 1988; OS 25-inch map about 1900)
items.why: The replica plans for the house are built from the 1974 measured ground plan (NA/GL/89/208) and the 1974 record card, which give the outline and the room sizes. RCAHMW NA/GL/88/49 records that the first floor and roof trusses could not be examined in 1974. No record held gives the heights, the roof pitch, the first-floor layout, the size of the 19th-century east extension, the door and window positions, the sizes and uses of the farm ranges, or the line of the yard and boundary walls. In the replica plans these values are inferred and marked so, with wide tolerances. Open question: whether any photograph, survey or plan from 1900 to 1988 records them.

items.title: Thomas v Hurst (1812-1813): the Chancery decree, the Master's report naming the buyers, and the sale particulars with their lot plan for the Llandough-juxta-Penarth freeholds
items.holder: Glamorgan Archives (the certified report: catalogue entry read, item not yet seen); The National Archives (the Court of Chancery's decree and order books for 1812-1814; not checked); the particulars and the estate map (whereabouts not known)
items.basis: practice (a sale under a Chancery decree: printed particulars and plan, the Master's report of the sale naming each buyer, and the order confirming it, entered in the court's books); cross-reference (The Cambrian, 26 June and 11 September 1813; Glamorgan Archives DART/W/70-92/79-84/82)
items.why: A Chancery decree of 21 July 1812, made in a creditors' suit over William Hurst's debts, ordered his freehold estates sold. The Cambrian of 26 June and 11 September 1813 advertised the sale of his freeholds in 'Landough juxta Penarth', St Andrews, Cadoxton, Merthyr Dyfan and Roath at the Cardiff Arms on 29 September 1813, with particulars and an estate map available from a firm of Cardiff solicitors. A certified report of the sale, dated 15 November 1813, is catalogued at Glamorgan Archives; its catalogue line names the buyer of lots 12 to 16 only. A sale under a Chancery decree was run before a Master, who reported each lot and its buyer, and the court confirmed the report by order, so the full lot list and the buyers should exist. These records do not name the house: whether any lot became part of the farm is not known. They would show who held the Llandough-juxta-Penarth land before the Bute estate's record of the farm begins in 1824. Parcel not identified (matching the lots' names and acreages against the c.1841 tithe, Llandough 196-267 and Leckwith 275-281, would identify any).
refs: Glamorgan Archives DART/W/70-92/79-84/82: certified report of sale, 15 November 1813 (lots 12-16 bought by Evan Thomas of Sully; other buyers not in the catalogue line)
The Cambrian, 26 June and 11 September 1813, p1: sale notice
Glamorgan Archives DXCE/3: 1793 Bute purchase of chief rents and advowsons (context; no farmland named)

items.title: Richards estate survey, 1777-1785: the Llandough page missing from the bound volume
items.status: NOT HELD: PAGES MISSING FROM THE VOLUME
items.holder: Glamorgan Archives (the volume, with pages 47-50 missing; date and cause of loss not known); any separated page or copy: not known
items.basis: cross-reference (Glamorgan Archives DPE/E/1 catalogue description: the volume's own index lists page 49 under Llandough; DXGL/9-10/9 map inset)
items.why: An estate survey of the Richards family's lands, made by Richards and Morgan between 1777 and 1785, is held at Glamorgan Archives as DPE/E/1. Its catalogue entry records: 'Pages 47-50 are missing and of those only page 49 appears in the index under Llandough'. A map inset elsewhere in the same archive (DXGL/9-10/9) marks 'Jn. Richard's esq.'s lands at Llandough', so the survey once carried a Llandough page. When and how the pages left the volume is not recorded in the catalogue line. This is a third-party estate record from before 1824; whether the Richards lands at Llandough included any Cedwyn parcel is not known. Parcel not identified (page 49 itself would identify the Richards lands at Llandough).
refs: Glamorgan Archives DPE/E/1: Richards and Morgan estate survey, 1777-1785 (catalogue description read)
Glamorgan Archives DXGL/9-10/9: map inset marking the Richards lands at Llandough
